chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the children who died before reaching adulthood?' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about them, so he said: Allah is more Knowing of what they were doing.' Then he turned towards me and said, 'O Zurara! Do you know what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) meant by that?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'He meant: Cease from judging them, and do not say anything regarding them, and refer their knowledge to Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Allah is more Knowing' regarding children who died before puberty?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the Prophet’s statement regarding pre-pubescent children, emphasizing the principle of 'kuww' (restraint) to prevent definitive claims about their eternal fate. This reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that while these children are not subject to the full burden of accountability (taklif), their ultimate destiny remains with Allah, discouraging both pessimistic and optimistic speculation. The hadith serves as a theological safeguard against overstepping divine knowledge in matters of individual salvation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the children who died before they reached adulthood?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was asked about them, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Knowing with what they were doing’. 
Then he<sup>asws</sup> turned towards me, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Zurara! Do you know what is the meaning of what Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said?’ I said, ‘No’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather it means pause from them and do not be saying anything regarding them, and refer their knowledge to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about children who die before maturity and he replied, ‘The Messenger of Allah was asked about them and he said, “Allah knows best about what they may do.’” Then he turned to me and said, ‘O Zurarah, do you know what the Messenger of Allah meant thereby?’ I said, ‘No, I do not know.’ He said, ‘He meant to say, “You must not say anything about them but leave their affairs to Allah (to deal with).’””
